title: WHEN A LEADER'S CONSCIENCE IS CLEAR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Moses became very angry and said to the Lord, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken so much as a donkey from them, nor have I wronged any of them." Moses said to Korah, "You and all your followers are to appear before the Lord tomorrow — you and they and Aaron. Each man is to take his censer and put incense in it — 250 censers in all — and present it before the Lord. You and Aaron are to present your censers also." — Num 16:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses is angry — and this is a righteous anger, provoked by a rebellion against God Himself. But notice how he pleads his integrity before the Lord: "I have not taken so much as a donkey from them, nor have I wronged any of them." Moses could look God in the face with a clear conscience. He had led without exploiting, served without enriching himself.

This is a beautiful and rare thing. Leaders are often tempted to use their position for personal gain — to take a little here, to bend things to their advantage there. Moses had refused all of it. His hands were clean. When accused of "lording it over" the people, he could truthfully say he had never taken advantage of a single one of them.

There is a challenge here for all of us, whether we lead many or few. Can we say our dealings with others have been honest and unselfish? Have we served people, or used them? A clear conscience before God is a treasure that no accusation can take away. When we have nothing to hide, we can face both God and our accusers with quiet confidence.

Moses' clean hands point us to One whose hands were perfectly clean — Jesus, who served without any self-interest at all, who came "not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many." Where every earthly leader falls short, Christ was the flawless Servant-King. And by His Spirit He shapes us into people of integrity, who serve others for their good and not for our own gain. Let us lead and live in such a way that our conscience is clear before God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you face God with a clear conscience in how you treat others?
2. Do you serve people for their good, or use them for your gain?
3. How does Jesus, the perfect Servant, inspire your own integrity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to live and serve with clean hands and a clear conscience. Keep me from ever using others for my own advantage. Make me like Christ, who came not to be served but to serve and to give His life for us. Amen.
